summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose to a record Rs1,370 crore-scale year with EBITDA up 22.5% to Rs144 crore; FY27 guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore.
summary.overview: Banswara Syntex reported Q4 FY26 total income of Rs369.3 crore, with EBITDA up 46% YoY to Rs46 crore and PAT of Rs9.6 crore (up 87% YoY). For FY26, EBITDA was about Rs144 crore (margin near 11%) and PAT Rs28.4 crore (up 32.8%) after a one-time Rs9 crore labour code exceptional charge. Fabric and Garment grew, while Yarn volumes and revenue fell on labour shortages in spinning. Management guided to FY27 revenue of Rs1,450-1,500 crore and EBITDA margin of 10.5-11% over the medium term, with near-term margin pressure from raw material pass-through lag.

financial_highlights.value: Rs28.4 crore (after Rs9 crore one-time labour code expense)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs456 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.value: 20% on face value, total Rs3.42 crore

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs113 crore (vs Rs123 crore; management corrected the gap to Rs10 crore), FY26 Rs449 crore vs Rs460 crore (about -2%). Volume 46 lakh kg in Q4 and 194 lakh kg in FY26; utilisation 78% in Q4 and 77% for FY26. Realisations up about Rs30-35/kg.

segments.name: Fabrics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs154 crore (vs Rs145 crore); FY26 record Rs569 crore, up 5%. Volume 62 lakh meters in Q4 and 230 lakh meters in FY26; utilisation 77% in Q4. Middle East exports affected.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue Rs96 crore, up 40%; FY26 Rs324 crore, up 18%. Volume 11 lakh pieces in Q4 and 39 lakh pieces in FY26; FY26 utilisation 72% vs about 50% in FY25. Walmart added about Rs15 crore of Q4 revenue.

segments.name: Associate Tesca Textiles (40% stake)
segments.commentary: Management said Tesca had turnover of about Rs100 crore and PAT of about Rs10 crore, with Banswara's share about Rs4 crore. No plan to raise stake.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs1,450-1,500 crore, led by Fabric and Garment; FY26 was about Rs1,370 crore.
Management targets about 20% revenue growth in both Fabric and Garment in FY27; Garment division projects 18-20%.
EBITDA margin expected at 10.5-11% over the medium term; near-term margins may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
FY27 capex planned at Rs135-140 crore (an analyst cited Rs130-150 crore); Garment capex only Rs3-5 crore.
Long-term debt expected to rise in FY27 on planned capex and reduce from FY28 onwards; no reduction in total borrowings this year.
Management expects H2 FY27 growth to exceed H1; Garment momentum to improve from Q2 after a subdued Q1.
capex_capacity: Yarn and Fabric capacity was reshaped toward finer counts, Siro Compact yarn (about 200 tons per month) and worsted finishing machines; management says installed capacity fell YoY partly due to mix shift.
Garment capacity: about 70,000 pieces per month available vs 40,000-50,000 jackets used; could go to 80,000 with long runs.
Surat SEZ garment capacity (about 40,000-50,000 jackets and about 100,000 pants) awaits approval; timeline not given, file under process with Industries Commissionerate and Kandla SEZ.
Management said Garment expansion could start mid-year (Q2/Q3 FY27) and that Rs2,000 crore revenue is possible without significant capex, with no firm timeline.
Capex items: zero water discharge project, a 132 KVA power line application, and other infrastructure and sustainability spend.
demand_pricing: Polyester raw material costs up about 25% due to the Middle East conflict; yarn prices raised but not fully passed on.
Wool prices rose sharply, from Australia and China; management says customers take 6 months to 1 year to accept new prices.
Rupee depreciation of about 6-7% helped export realisations without price increases.
Walmart added as a Garment customer; JC Penney (Fabric) and Mango (Garment) already customers; Celio and Marks & Spencer cited as large relationships.
Middle East exposure about Rs100 crore; Rs8-9 crore of Q4 product could not ship on time; management expects Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region in FY27.
US demand improving; company says it is more competitive than China in spun-synthetic segment.
D2C brand One Mile averages about Rs15 lakh per month; fundraising planned once it reaches about Rs1 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Have new export clients been added, such as Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Walmart is a new addition; it contributed about Rs15 crore of Q4 Garment revenue. Management aims for 20% growth in Garment and Fabric next year and sees no need for many more large clients.

qa_highlights.question: Why did installed capacity fall YoY despite investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Finer counts and worsted machines lower kg output; capacity is planned around realistic labour availability. Management says labour shortages persist into May.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage transient or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says automation is not viable given many SKUs; focus is on scaling winning products and shifting from made-to-order to predictive analytics planning.

qa_highlights.question: How will the borrowings be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no reduction in FY27 as long-term debt rises on capex; long-term debt to reduce from FY28 on 5-7 year loan tenures. Working capital rise is linked to customer ready inventory; inventory above 90 days is watched.

qa_highlights.question: What are segment-wise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give exact segment margins due to internal transfers (about 33% of yarn and 25% of fabric is internal). Segment margins are said to be close to company level; Garment was previously at breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said polyester costs rose about 25%; price increases partly accepted, and export pricing benefited from rupee weakness. Middle East exposure is about Rs100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will FTAs (UK, EU) matter, and can Rs1,800 crore be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: UK FTA expected around September and EU by December end per management, with no certainty. Management hopes for Rs1,800 crore in the year after FY27 and is willing to accept 11% EBITDA to keep 20% growth.

risks_watch: Labour shortages in spinning and garments, particularly in April to June, could keep Yarn utilisation at 77-78%.
Raw material cost pass-through lag of 6 to 12 months may compress margins in H1 FY27.
Middle East logistics and demand; Rs10-20 crore lower sales to the region expected in FY27.
Surat SEZ approval timing is uncertain, and no firm Garment capacity expansion date was given.
Net debt rose to Rs483 crore; the long-term debt reduction only starts from FY28, while FY27 capex is Rs135-140 crore.
FTA benefits (UK, EU) are not yet certain; Q1 FY27 Garment orders expected to be subdued.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Garment growth and export wins, but cautious on near-term margins, Q1 FY27 demand, and the Middle East. Management avoided firm timelines on Surat SEZ, FTAs and the Rs2,000 crore revenue target, and declined to give segment margins.
key_quotes: So, we are happy even if we get 11% EBITDA, but we grow 20% for this present financial year because we do not want to stifle the growth by jacking up the prices to an extent where the customers shy away.
Walmart has been definitely a new addition, and we saw the impact of that happening in our quarter four results in the Garment division, where we achieved INR96 crores turnover.
Near-term margins may go down as the raw material costs are being passed on.
